<break time="0.8s" /> Twenty more than his due. <break time="0.8s" /> Telling him that he must go. <break time="0.8s" /> Proud of my masterly management. <break time="0.8s" /> In assuming his departure. <break time="0.8s" /> I returned the next morning. <break time="0.8s" /> Only to hear. <break time="0.8s" /> From behind the screen. <break time="0.8s" /> The same mild voice reply. <break time="0.8s" /> I would prefer not to quit you. <break time="0.8s" /> Seized for a moment by a dangerous anger. <break time="0.8s" /> I recalled. <break time="0.8s" /> How a hasty man in a lonely office. <break time="0.8s" /> Had once lost his temper. <break time="0.8s" /> And committed a dreadful deed. <break time="0.8s" /> And I calmed myself. <break time="0.8s" /> With the thought of charity. <break time="0.8s" /> After reading Edwards on the Will and Priestley on Necessity. <break time="0.8s" /> I came to believe. <break time="0.8s" /> That Bartleby had been billeted upon me. <break time="0.8s" /> For some mysterious purpose. <break time="0.8s" /> Of an all wise Providence. <break time="0.8s" /> But my professional friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Visiting the office. <break time="0.8s" /> Began to whisper. <break time="0.8s" /> About the strange creature I kept there. <break time="0.8s" /> And a rumor spread. <break time="0.8s" /> That he might outlive me. <break time="0.8s" /> And claim possession of my office. <break time="0.8s" /> By right of his perpetual occupancy. <break time="0.8s" /> Since he would not leave me. <break time="0.8s" /> I resolved to leave him. <break time="0.8s" /> And so I moved my offices. <break time="0.8s" /> To another building. <break time="0.8s" /> Saying to him at parting. <break time="0.8s" /> Good bye, Bartleby, and God some way bless you. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon the new tenant and the landlord. <break time="0.8s" /> Came to me in despair. <break time="0.8s" /> For Bartleby. <break time="0.8s" /> Refusing to depart. <break time="0.8s" /> Now sat upon the banister of the stairs by day. <break time="0.8s" /> And slept in the entry by night. <break time="0.8s" /> I offered him one occupation after another. <break time="0.8s" /> A clerkship in a store. <break time="0.8s" /> A bartenders post. <break time="0.8s" /> A trip to Europe as a companion. <break time="0.8s" /> And finally my own home. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet he would prefer. <break time="0.8s" /> Not to make any change at all.
